static_traits.name: He Yating
static_traits.family_status: Likes dining out with family, but tension arises during family outings due to anxiety and frustration
static_traits.social_status: Social life is affected; has family to confide in but they do not fully understand the depth of the anxiety
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous psychological counseling or treatment experience; no similar problems related to dining out before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to concretely describe thinking patterns, bodily sensations, and emotions; high cooperation, positive attitude; good logic; speech rate and verbal fluency not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I often believe that every time I go to a certain restaurant they will get my order wrong, which makes me feel frustrated and anxious.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent anxiety and frustration have markedly affected my quality of life and my enjoyment of social activities, so I hope to reduce meal-related anxiety through counseling and once again enjoy dining out and socializing with family.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, at a particular restaurant, my order was gotten wrong several times in a row; the stress was moderate at first, but it gradually escalated into generalized anxiety about and avoidance of dining out; I tried communicating with the staff and changing the way I ordered, but in my view the problem persisted; after that I began to avoid this restaurant and to feel nervous about dining out overall, which led to misunderstandings and tension when dining out with family; although there were occasionally smooth dining experiences, these positive experiences were hard to retain in my memory.

core_beliefs: They will never get my order right
Something always goes wrong when dining out

special_situations.event: Last weekend, planned to go to a new restaurant and prepared to eat out
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the restaurant gets the order wrong, the whole outing will be ruined and I will be very anxious and upset
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Suggesting eating at home, directly avoiding dining out
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will get my order wrong; this will ruin everything

special_situations.event: Each time considering dining out, especially thinking of that restaurant that has made mistakes many times
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past several consecutive times of being gotten wrong means it will continue to happen in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding that restaurant and broadly reducing dining out

special_situations.event: When recalling past experiences of orders being mixed up, focuses only on the negative events and ignores the few smooth meals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive experiences are not worth referencing, only experiences of making mistakes explain the problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent worry, repeatedly replaying negative experiences in the mind
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Good experiences mean nothing; problems will always happen

special_situations.event: Before ordering or lacking specific information, being convinced the waiter will make a mistake again
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must prepare for the worst in advance to avoid being struck down by mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Changing the order in advance, communicating with staff many times to try to control the outcome
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will get it wrong this time too

core_conflict.wish: Longs for a relaxed, predictable dining experience where one is treated well, and to spend enjoyable time with family
core_conflict.fear: Fears uncontrollable external mistakes will ruin the experience and family atmosphere, triggering strong anxiety and frustration
defense_goal: Reduces uncertainty and anxiety by avoiding dining out and controlling details in advance

object_relations.self_representation: A tense diner easily affected when things go wrong outside

manifestations: Family does not fully understand the depth of one's anxiety
Misunderstandings and tension arise during family outings due to their tension and irritability
Reducing socializing and dining out due to anxiety
outcomes: Expanding avoidance, declining quality of life
Anxiety and tension generalize to social settings

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to change thinking patterns and try reality testing
Maintaining communication with family, although understanding is limited there is still some support
Objectively, there are a few experiences of meals going smoothly as counter-evidence
Has proactively communicated with restaurant staff and adjusted the way of ordering, showing willingness to solve problems
negative_force: Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, and fortune-telling maintain anxiety
Ignoring and disqualifying positive experiences intensifies negative expectations
Anticipatory anxiety accompanied by increased heart rate and strong tension
Avoidance behavior leads to reduced social and family outings, decreased quality of life

antecedent: Planning to go to that restaurant that has made mistakes many times
Family members suggest going out for a meal
target_behavior.core_reason: Stems from several consecutive negative experiences of orders being gotten wrong, forming catastrophizing and overgeneralizing predictions that 'things will always go wrong'
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential mistakes and uncomfortable emotions to lower anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Social life and eating habits change, family outings decrease with tension arising, and overall quality of life declines

target_behavior.behavior: Meal-related anticipatory anxiety and physical reactions (faster heart rate, tension, apprehension, irritability)
antecedent: Considering going to a restaurant or starting to plan dining out
Recalling past experiences of orders being gotten wrong
As the time to dine out approaches
target_behavior.core_reason: Predictions of inevitable future mistakes and mental filtering of negative experiences lead to emotional reasoning and heightened vigilance
target_behavior.function: Attempts to control uncertainty by increasing vigilance and worry (but actually reinforces anxiety)
target_behavior.consequence: Present experience and enjoyment of time with family decline, irritability increases and triggers misunderstandings and tension
